archetypes.name: consumer-stub-completeness
archetypes.rationale: The plan updates three design consumer scripts to parse COMBINED_FALLBACK_COUNT but omits their unit test harnesses (test-dispatch-plan-review-panel.sh and test-decompose-panel-dispatch.sh), which contain waterfall output stubs that emit only FALLBACK_COUNT — leaving the new parse path silently unexercised and the degradation comparison swap untestable.
archetypes.prompt_body: For every script the plan modifies to parse a new KV from dispatcher output, locate the corresponding test harness stub that synthesizes that output and verify whether the stub is updated to emit the new key. Specifically, check whether `skills/design/scripts/test-dispatch-plan-review-panel.sh` and `skills/design/scripts/test-decompose-panel-dispatch.sh` include `COMBINED_FALLBACK_COUNT` (and `PHASE2_RELAUNCH_COUNT`) in their `printf`/`W_STUB_*` stub emitters, since both harnesses currently emit only `FALLBACK_COUNT`. If stubs are absent from the plan's modification list, flag the gap: the defensive fallback will silently mask the new parse path during consumer unit tests, meaning the degradation-comparison swap from `FALLBACK_COUNT` to `COMBINED_FALLBACK_COUNT` could regress without a test catching it. Also verify the plan's conditional language around `make test-dispatch-plan-review-panel` and `make test-decompose-panel-dispatch` — check whether those Makefile targets actually exist and whether the plan's omission of the stub files from the modification list is a gap rather than an intentional scope choice. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
